title: Weaving a Future: How a Young Weaver Keeps Bamboo Craft Alive
title_zh: 编织未来：一位年轻编织者如何让竹编手艺延续
intro_zh: 本文约501词，适合CET-4水平。文章以四川竹编为例，讲述年轻传承人如何通过网店、短视频和工作坊，让传统手工艺在当代焕发新生。

paragraphs.en: In a small village in Sichuan, China, the sound of thin bamboo strips clicking against each other fills the morning air. For centuries, families here have woven baskets, hats, and trays from bamboo. This skill is part of their heritage. But today, fewer young people want to learn it. The craft is in danger of disappearing.
paragraphs.zh: 在中国四川的一个小村庄里，细竹条相互碰撞的声音填满了清晨的空气。几个世纪以来，这里的家庭都用竹子编织篮子、帽子和托盘。这项技能是他们遗产的一部分。但如今，愿意学习它的年轻人越来越少。这门手艺正面临消失的危险。

paragraphs.en: One person who refused to let it fade is Li Wei, a 28-year-old weaver. After working in a city office for three years, he returned home. He missed the quiet rhythm of village life. 'I saw my grandfather's hands move like magic,' he says. 'I wanted to keep that magic alive.' He became an apprentice to his uncle, a master weaver.
paragraphs.zh: 拒绝让它消失的人是28岁的编织者李伟。在城里的办公室工作三年后，他回到了家乡。他怀念乡村生活安静的节奏。“我看到祖父的手像魔法一样移动，”他说。“我想让那种魔法活下去。”他成了舅舅——一位编织大师——的学徒。

paragraphs.en: Learning bamboo weaving is not easy. It takes months to master basic technique. Li practiced eight hours a day, cutting bamboo into strips as thin as a thread. His fingers bled at first. 'Many friends gave up,' he says. 'But I told myself I had to preserve this skill.'
paragraphs.zh: 学习竹编并不容易。掌握基本技巧需要几个月。李每天练习八个小时，把竹子切成细如线的条。起初他的手指流了血。“很多朋友放弃了，”他说。“但我告诉自己，我必须保护这门技艺。”

paragraphs.en: Traditionally, woven bamboo items were sold at local markets for low prices. A large basket might earn only 30 yuan. Young people left for better-paying jobs. 'My generation didn't see a future in it,' Li explains. The number of full-time weavers in his village dropped from over 200 in 1990 to fewer than 30 in 2020.
paragraphs.zh: 传统上，竹编物品在当地市场上以低价出售。一个大篮子可能只卖30元。年轻人离开去从事收入更高的工作。“我这一代人在其中看不到未来，”李解释说。他村里的全职编织者人数从1990年的200多人下降到2020年的不到30人。

paragraphs.en: Li decided to change that. He opened an online shop and posted short videos of his work. The shop now ships about 200 items each month. In one video, he wove a delicate butterfly from bamboo. It received 2 million views. Orders came from as far as Germany and Australia. He also started weekend workshops for tourists. 'People love to touch the bamboo and try weaving themselves,' he says.
paragraphs.zh: 李决定改变这种状况。他开了一家网店，并发布自己作品的短视频。这家店现在每月发货约200件。在一个视频中，他用竹子编织了一只精致的蝴蝶。它获得了200万次观看。订单远至德国和澳大利亚。他还为游客开设了周末工作坊。“人们喜欢触摸竹子，尝试自己编织，”他说。

paragraphs.en: Local schools now invite Li to teach students. He has shown over 1,000 children how to make simple bamboo stars. 'When a child finishes a star, their eyes light up,' he says. 'That is the start of a revival.' The government also lists bamboo weaving as an intangible cultural heritage, offering small grants to young weavers.
paragraphs.zh: 当地学校现在邀请李教学生。他已经向1000多名儿童展示了如何制作简单的竹星。“当一个孩子完成一颗星时，他们的眼睛会亮起来，”他说。“那就是复兴的开始。”政府还将竹编列为非物质文化遗产，为年轻编织者提供小额资助。

paragraphs.en: But challenges remain. Bamboo weaving still cannot match factory wages. Li earns about 4,000 yuan a month, less than many of his friends. 'Sometimes I worry about money,' he admits. 'But when I see a finished piece, I feel rich.' To support young weavers, the local government offers free studio space and low-interest loans.
paragraphs.zh: 但挑战依然存在。竹编仍然无法与工厂工资相比。李每月挣大约4000元，比他的许多朋友都少。“有时我会为钱担心，”他承认。“但当我看到一件完成的作品时，我感到富有。”为了支持年轻编织者，当地政府提供免费工作室空间和低息贷款。

paragraphs.en: Li's story is not unique. Across China, from tie-dye in Yunnan to paper-cutting in Shaanxi, young people are using new tools—phones, cameras, and online platforms—to share old skills. They mix traditional designs with modern tastes. A bamboo phone case, for example, sells for 120 yuan, far more than a plain basket.
paragraphs.zh: 李的故事并不独特。在中国各地，从云南的扎染到陕西的剪纸，年轻人正在使用新工具——手机、相机和在线平台——来分享古老技能。他们将传统设计与现代品味相结合。例如，一个竹制手机壳售价120元，远高于一个普通篮子。

paragraphs.en: 'Tradition is not a museum piece,' Li says. 'It must live in daily life.' By teaching, innovating, and connecting with the world, he and others are proving that old crafts can find new hands. The clicking of bamboo strips continues—not as a memory, but as a promise for the future. That promise is already taking shape.
paragraphs.zh: “传统不是博物馆里的展品，”李说。“它必须活在日常生活中。”通过教学、创新和与世界连接，他和其他人正在证明，古老的手艺可以找到新的双手。竹条的咔嗒声继续着——不是作为记忆，而是作为对未来的承诺。这一承诺已经在成形。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Bamboo weaving is too difficult for young people to learn.
A young weaver is using new ways to keep a traditional craft alive.
The Chinese government has banned the sale of bamboo baskets.
Traditional crafts are disappearing because of online shopping.
questions.explain: 文章主要讲述李伟如何通过网店、视频和工作坊传承竹编，并带动其他年轻人复兴传统手工艺，因此B项最符合主旨。

questions.q: What happened to the number of full-time weavers in Li Wei's village between 1990 and 2020?
options: It dropped from over 200 to fewer than 30.
questions.explain: 文章第四段明确提到，全职编织者从1990年的200多人下降到2020年的不到30人，故选C。

questions.q: What can we infer about Li Wei from the passage?
options: He regrets leaving his city job.
He earns more than his friends who work in factories.
He believes traditional crafts should stay unchanged.
He finds personal satisfaction in his work despite lower income.
questions.explain: 第七段提到他虽然收入比朋友低，有时担心钱，但看到成品时感到富有，说明他从工作中获得满足感，故选D。

questions.q: The word 'revival' in Paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: revival意为“复兴、复苏”，与“coming back to life”意思最接近，故选A。
